Document Overview & Structure
This underwriting and rating manual outlines the actuarial procedures, classification classifications, ter-
ritorial relativities, exposure bases, schedule modification plans, and sequential premium calculation
algorithms applicable to Apex Mutual’s Commercial General Liability (CGL) product lines.
Notice Regarding Document Validation & Parsing Systems
This document contains rigorous structural logic intended to benchmark document intelligence and rules
engine extractors:
•Mathematical Chain Determinism:Sequential procedures follow strict variable assignment pat-
terns, rounding rules, intermediate accumulator tracking, and rate capping.
•Syntactical Cross-Referencing:All rating routines explicitly call lookup tables, classification sched-
ules, deductible scales, and endorsement modifiers.
•Designated Document Discrepancies:Under Sections10and11, specific rules and table cells con-
tain intentional contradictions, boundary overlaps, or unpopulated values designed to test system
error trapping rather than silent reconciliation.

1 Statutory Definitions and Operational Exposure Bases
1.1Standard Policy Definitions
For the purposes of this manual and all associated rating routines, the capitalized terms below have
specific defined meanings.
Premises/Operations Liability (Prem/Ops): Liability coverage for accidental bodily injury (BI) or prop-
erty damage (PD) sustained by third parties arising out of the insured’s physical business locations
or direct on-going operational activities.
Products/Completed Operations (Prod/Comp): Liability coverage for third-party bodily injury or prop-
erty damage arising out of goods or products manufactured, sold, handled, or distributed once
physical possession has been relinquished, or operations completed away from the insured’s premises.
Basic Policy Limits (BPL):The standard baseline limit against which basic rates are quoted, defined
strictly as $100,000 Each Occurrence / $200,000 General Aggregate / $200,000 Products-Completed
Operations Aggregate, with $5,000 Medical Payments.
Increased Limit Factor (ILF):A multiplicative actuarial factor applied to the basic limit rate to generate
the premium required for policy limits exceeding the standard BPL.
Experience Modification Factor (EMF):A mandatory factor derived from the insured’s past three com-
plete policy years of audited loss experience compared against industry expected losses.
Schedule Rating Factor (SRF):An underwriter-discretionary modifier reflecting unique physical, man-
agement, or risk control characteristics, constrained within statutory limits.
1.2Exposure Bases and Units of Measure
Rating algorithms require quantifying the insured risk using standardized exposure bases. Every classi-
fication code corresponds to one of the following exposure dimensions:

2 Classification Schedule and Base Rates
The classification codes listed in Table2establish the primary operational group, governing exposure
base, hazard rating grade, and base rates per unit of exposure for standard BPL ($100,000/$200,000).
2.1Classification Assignment Principles
1.Single-Operation Assignment:If an insured entity engages in one predominant commercial ac-
tivity, the entire exposure must be assigned to that specific classification code.
2.Multi-Operation Split Rules:If distinct operational divisions maintain fully segregated accounting,
payroll, and sales books, exposures may be segregated by code. Under no circumstances may
contracting operational payroll be split between high-hazard and low-hazard codes unless daily
time-card tracking is maintained.
3.General Inclusions:Operational payroll must include active foremen, shipping personnel, ware-
house staff, and internal maintenance teams under the primary operational code.

3 Territory Relativities and Geographic Factors
Every commercial exposure must be rated according to its physical operating territory. Territorial bound-
aries reflect litigation frequency, judicial climate, municipal building densities, and historical claim sever-
ities.
3.1Territorial Application Directives
•Premises Exposure: Rated strictly by the territorial code where the real property is physically situ-
ated.
•Operations Exposure (Contractors): Rated by the territory where the contracting activities are
performed. If contractors operate across multiple territorial zones, payroll must be allocated pro-
portionally; unallocated contractor payroll must be assigned to the highest-rated operating terri-
tory.
•Products Liability:Products/Completed Operations coverage applies a blended statewide factor
based on corporate headquarters location.

5 Experience Rating Plan
The Experience Rating Plan adjusts standard manual premium to reflect the insured’s individual loss
experience. Participation is mandatory for any commercial risk whose annual basic manual premium
equals or exceeds $5,000.
5.1Experience Eligibility and Historical Experience Period
The experience period consists of the three completed policy years immediately preceding the current
renewal year. If three complete years are unavailable, two consecutive years may be utilized, provided
subject premium exceeds $10,000 in aggregate.
5.2Actuarial Valuation Formula
The Experience Modification Factor (EM F ) is computed via the credibility-weighted formula:
EM F =
Ap+Ce·Ep+ (1-Ce)·Ee
